parts.text:
A student constructed a table to compare the structural features of a plant cell, a prokaryotic cell and a virus.

Complete Table 6.1.

Table 6.1

| feature | plant cell | prokaryotic cell | virus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| external structure | cell wall composed of cellulose | cell wall composed of | capsid composed of |
| size of ribosomes | $80\text{S}$ and $70\text{S}$ |  | no ribosomes |
| nucleic acids | DNA and RNA | DNA and RNA |  |

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The cholera bacterium releases a protein toxin called choleragen. The toxin causes the loss of chloride ions and water from epithelial cells into the lumen of the intestine.

Fig. 6.1 shows the events that occur in cells lining the intestine when choleragen binds to the membrane of one of these cells.

{{figure:figure_6_1.webp}}

Fig. 6.1

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State **one** likely source of an outbreak of cholera.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 6.1, state why choleragen molecules are described as having quaternary structure.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the type of cell membrane component that forms the receptor for choleragen.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The process by which chloride ions leave the epithelial cell requires energy.

Name the phosphorylated nucleotide that is needed for this process.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Explain why water also moves from epithelial cells into the lumen of the intestine when choleragen is present.
